start: ^Narrator: A woman in her mid-forties looks up from a whiteboard dense with lattice notation.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: You're the consultant. Ruth Halloran. I run Heisenberg.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Find whoever did this, and quickly. And I hope to God you're wrong about my team.
^Walk me through what was taken. It'll help me narrow it down.
^I need to talk to everyone with access to Heisenberg.
^Could you have missed someone behaving differently?

c-1: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: My team didn't do this.
c-2: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: I know my people.

heisenberg_explanation: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Heisenberg is quantum-safe key exchange for the new national emergency dispatch network. The system that routes nine-nine-nine calls.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Lattice-based, built to survive a quantum computer. That's a problem for the 2030s. Tonight's problem is simpler.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: The keys rotate region by region during the rollout. Hold the keys, know the windows, and you don't need to break anything. You wait.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: People could die waiting for an ambulance. I've done the arithmetic. I try not to look at it.

defensive_response: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: My team are brilliant, and vetted to the hilt.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: If one of them did this, somebody gave them a reason. Pressure. Coercion.
^I'm not here to judge. Whoever did this might be a victim too.
^A reason doesn't make it right. They made a choice.

c-0: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Thank you. Not many in your line would say that.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: The police have David. Nobody's told me anything else.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: David put his head round my door on his way out. He said thank you, and went.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: I've rung David twice. He's not answering.
^ I'm to treat David as normal on Monday. I don't know how I'll manage that.

hub: ^What can you tell me about David Torres?
^Your spare badge has been through the server hallway at night. Four times.
^I need into the server hallway. Your badge opens it.
^The key vault takes your thumbprint. Could someone have lifted it?

c-8: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Good luck. I mean that.

ask_team_members: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Eight people. I hired most of them myself.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Amara and Tomasz could rebuild the key exchange from memory. David Torres is my cryptography lead, the best I've worked with.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Ben's frightened of falling behind. David's had a hard year at home. I've carried both of them.

ask_torres: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: David made Heisenberg work. Two years of his life are in that key exchange.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: I've watched him fight the insurer for months. Every denial letter, he'd come in next morning and work twice as hard.

ask_vault: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Off me? Not in this lab. Gloves at the bench, always; it's the first rule I wrote.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: You'll not lift anything of mine in here. Try it if you like.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: You've been straight with me. Here, the visitor spare. It's signed out through me, and I'm signing it out to you.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: It's registered to me, and it opens the server hallway. Bring it back when you're done.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: I don't know you well enough to hand you my access.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Owen in IT can sort you out, if it's that urgent.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Security have given me my access back. I'll want an apology from you. Not tonight.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Patricia's given me my access back. I'll want an apology from you. Not tonight.

accused_greeting: ^Narrator: Dr Halloran sits at her bench with her coat on, as if she's been told to wait.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Security have suspended my access. I'm to wait here for the police. On your say-so, I gather.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Ask what you came to ask.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: You could have asked me this before you rang Security.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: The one you're carrying. It's signed out through me, and I've never signed it out at night.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: My spare? It's the visitor spare, signed out through me. I haven't signed it out in months.

spare_badge: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: The twenty-third I was in Zurich, giving a paper to two hundred people. The lanyard's on my monitor.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Who's in here after hours? Amara some evenings, gone by ten. Ben, for his test runs. David, some nights; he says it's quieter than his office.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Any of them could have walked out with it. I never thought to count.

b: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Security have given me my access back. I'll want an apology from you. Not tonight.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: Patricia's given me my access back. I'll want an apology from you. Not tonight.

halloran_guilt: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: I should have seen it. He was pulling away. Working late, alone. Avoiding my eye.
^Dr Ruth Halloran: I signed his overtime every week and never once asked what it was for.
^ENTROPY picked him because he was drowning. That isn't on you.

c-0: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: It doesn't help. Thank you anyway.
c-1: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: He did. So did they, when they picked him.

torres_defense: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: What happens to him now?
^That depends on whether he helps us.

c-0: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: Then think about his circumstances when you're in front of him. Please.
c-1: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: It was never in yours. Mine, maybe.
c-2: ^Dr Ruth Halloran: *quietly* I suppose he will.
